applies_to: v2 (physics-first reimplementation) vs the stock Fortran (ATLAS9/DFSYNTHE/KAPPA9/SYNTHE), with the same input physics and data; stage-isolated (each stage gets the stock upstream products).

evidence_kinds.cross-code upper bound: Differences between different codes; quoted only as an upper bound.
evidence_kinds.derived: Propagated from a supported tolerance by stated physics, or bounded between a self-consistency level and a cross-code level.
evidence_kinds.reimplementation: Published same-physics reimplementations of the Kurucz codes validated against the Fortran (pyKurucz, Payne Zero). The closest analogue to v2.
evidence_kinds.self-consistency: Numerical precision or convergence level of a single code (convergence criteria, frequency-sampling tests, same-code scheme changes). Preferred.
evidence_kinds.unsupported: No literature support found; value proposed and marked.

frozen: 2026-11-04, before any v2 output existed; never edit to make a score pass
metric_conventions: Keys follow src/atlas_torch/scoring.py: rel = max |a-b|/max(|a|,|b|); abs in the quantity's own units; rms_* = rms of the same pointwise error. ODF/kapk tolerances are given in dex; the scorer works in 0.001-dex steps (multiply by 1000). 'v*' = every vturb (0,1,2,4,8). tol=null means not gated. Keys marked proposed_new_metric are not yet in scoring.py.
not_found: No refereed number for absolute (non-normalised) synthetic flux agreement between same-physics implementations; cont/flux tolerances are derived.
No published per-step ODF tolerance; ODF per-entry gates are unsupported proposals.
Kurucz 2005, MSAIS 8, 73 ('Physical, numerical, and computational limits for Kurucz codes') could not be retrieved (host unreachable) and is not cited.
No published HEIGHT or radiative/convective-split tolerance.

derived_labels_vs_fortran.basis: Optional end-to-end check: fit v2 spectra with Fortran-generated spectra, or the reverse. Payne Zero's reimplementation induces a bias of at most 4.6 K in Teff, 0.013 dex in log g and 0.011 dex in [M/H] when fitting the original Kurucz spectra. Proposed: [X/H] <= 0.02 dex, Teff <= 10 K, log g <= 0.02 dex. Different radiative-transfer codes with the same inputs differ by up to 0.05-0.12 dex (Jofre et al.); that is an upper bound only.

FLXERR:abs.also_require: v2 max|FLXERR| < 1 over log tau_Ross in [-4,1]
FLXERR:abs.basis: Units: percent, as printed by ATLAS9. A model counts as converged in the ATLAS9 literature when |flux error| < 1% at all depths (log tau_Ross -4..1); BasicATLAS GOLD uses the same rule. Two models that both meet the criterion are equivalent at this level, so the primary gate is that v2's own best iteration satisfies max|FLXERR| < 1. Separately, |dFLXERR| vs the Fortran must be <= 1 percentage point. The MARCS same-code sampling error in flux integrals (<1.5%) supports the same order.

HEIGHT:abs.basis: No literature number. Proposed: |dh| <= 0.01 x (max HEIGHT - min HEIGHT) of the reference model, scale-free across dwarfs and giants (needs a scorer change). It follows from the about 1% density tolerance integrated over the atmosphere.

P:rel.basis: MARCS converges log P corrections to <0.01 dex (2.3%), which caps the numerical noise of a converged model. P(tau) = integral of g/kappa dtau, so it inherits an averaged kappa error (well below the local 2%). The cross-code MARCS-ATLAS9 difference of 2-3% must sit above a same-physics tolerance, hence 1%.
P:rel.evidence: derived; bounded by self-consistency and cross-code

T:rel.basis: Score log tau_Ross in [-4, 1] (the layers Meszaros et al. used for ATLAS9 convergence); outside that range, report only. Same-code numerical levels: MARCS sampling errors are about 0.002 Teff for grid models; Payne Zero's change of the Kurucz line-selection fraction moves T by up to 5.9 K (about 0.1%); its stopping test is 5e-4 in the deep layers. Upper bounds: MARCS vs ATLAS9 cross-code is <1% (10-80 K at the surface of giants); interpolated vs direct models differ by 2-3%. Compiler-level reruns of ATLAS9 give 0.1-0.2 K, which is bit-level noise, not the v2 target. 2e-3 is about 11 K at T = 5777 K, about 9 K at the solar surface and about 20 K at T = 10000 K.

TAUROS:rel.basis: ATLAS9 output layers sit on its fixed log tau_Ross grid, so this checks that v2 uses the same grid, not physics. Proposed: print precision plus margin.

XNE:rel.basis: Saha sensitivity: d ln Ne / d ln T is about chi/(2kT), roughly 9 for metal donors at the solar photosphere, so the 2e-3 T tolerance maps to about 2%. This matches MARCS's 0.01 dex (2.3%) pressure-convergence level. The cross-code MARCS-ATLAS9 difference of 2-3% is the upper bound.

logkappa_ros:abs.basis: Rosseland-mean tables: halving or thinning the frequency grid in one code changes log kappa_R by about ±0.05 dex over most of (T, R) (AESOPUS App. B), and independent opacity codes agree mostly within ±0.05 dex. Rerunning Castelli's DFSYNTHE/KAPPA9 scripts gives perfect agreement within numerical precision, but that is a same-binary check, not the v2 target. Note: this project's own compiler variants of stock DFSYNTHE already differ by up to 0.015 dex, so a tolerance below about 0.02 dex would be unattainable even for Fortran.

_functional_gate.note: The defensible ODF acceptance test is functional: (1) logkappa_ros within 0.05 dex, and (2) an ATLAS9 model converged with v2 ODFs vs the same model with Fortran ODFs passes every atlas tolerance above. This is the use the ODF is designed for ('accurate enough for solving integrals over frequency in model atmosphere computations').

odf_v*:abs.basis: Not gated: per-step maxima are threshold-dominated (see p999).

odf_v*:p999.basis: Proposed 100 steps at the 99.9th percentile. Single steps can jump when a line crosses DFSYNTHE's 0.001*kappa_c inclusion threshold; per-entry maxima are not physically meaningful (this project's stock-vs-ifx-precise noise floor reaches 3.6 dex in 0.35% of entries).

odf_v*:rms_abs.basis: One ODF step = 0.001 dex (Kurucz packs log opacity in 2-byte integers). Proposed 10 steps rms, from Kurucz's 0.1-1% precision target for line data (0.0004-0.004 dex) with margin.

_resolution.basis: The same-physics validations of Kurucz reimplementations compare on the native synthesis grid (R = 300000 in both papers). cont:rel.basis: Neither reimplementation reports the absolute continuum. flux:rel.basis: Not gated. The scorer divides by max(|Fa|,|Fb|), which is ill-conditioned in saturated cores: the stock 380-420 nm window has normalised flux down to 0.0 (p0.1 = 0.015), so a 1e-2 normflux difference there becomes a relative difference of order 1. No paper bounds relative absolute flux in line cores. Gate absolute flux with flux_over_cont:abs instead.

flux:rms_rel.basis: Rms is dominated by continuum-level pixels, so it is bounded by cont:rms_rel + normflux:rms_abs, about 3e-3. Proposed 2e-3 because the two errors are correlated through the shared continuum.

These residuals reflect small numerical differences between two implementations of the same physical calculation.

normflux:abs.basis: Max |Fa/Ca - Fb/Cb|. Closest analogues are two independent reimplementations of Kurucz SYNTHE (same physics, same line data) validated against the Fortran: pyKurucz has sub-1% maxima, and Payne Zero's worst 99th percentile is 5.8e-3, so its maxima are of order 1e-2. Payne Zero shows that SYNTHE's own 1e-3 line-selection cutoff already moves the spectrum by about 3e-3 rms. Both papers compare at native sampling (R = 300000), not after degradation, so we score at the native R = 600000 grid. Extra risk at R = 600000 and in 380-420 nm (Payne Zero's residuals grow towards the blue) is covered by taking the maxima bound and not the p99.
